newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIA MUST URGE CHINA TO HOLD H.K. ELECTIONS: DOWNER
Foreign Affairs minister Alexander Downer says Australia is urging China to stick to its commitment to hold elections for the Hong Kong legislature as soon as possible.
The leader of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, Martin Lee, says Australia is morally obliged to follow the US lead in boycotting the swearing-in of Beijing's un-elected legislature.
Mr Downer says Australia will make up its own mind about attending the handover ceremony.
Mr Downer has told ABC Radio China is not flagging the provisional legislature as a permanent arrangement, but is committed to having election for a permanent Legislative Council.
He says to argue that the Provisional Legislative Council marks the death of democracy is hyperbole designed to generate a headline.
INQUIRY INTO NCA ADJOURNS OVER ARGUMENT
The Senate inquiry into the National Crime Authority was forced to adjourn for a time this morning when an argument broke out over a line of questioning directed at businessman John Elliott.
Labor Senator Steven Conroy split the committeee by pursuing a controversial line of inquiry regarding specific transactions while questioning Mr Elliott.
Mr Elliott refused to respond to his questions, accusing Senator Conroy of showing political bias.
Committee chairman and Liberal MP, John Bradford, adjourned the meeting to determine whether the questions were appropriate. The Committee later reconvened, with the specific questioning continuing.
PROTESTANT ASSOCIATION REGRETS ANY ABUSE OF CHILDREN
The United Protestant Association says it's willing to help any former residents who were abused while in its care.
A former UPA volunteer has alleged children at one of the Association's boys homes in Sydney were treated appallingly in the early 1970's.
Marion Le claims boys were drugged, not fed and clothed properly, beaten and at one stage deserted when staff walked out on them for a week.
General Manager Steven Walkerden says the Association deeply regrets any instances of abuse of children in its care, and is willing to assist any who contact it.
Although the UPA still operates children's institutions throughout New South Wales, the one in question has since been closed down.
HEALTH AND RESEARCH COUNCIL WORRIED DRUG TRIALS COULD SUFFER
The National Health and Medical Research Council is worried people will be deterred from taking part in human trials of drugs because of publicity about the use of orphans in post-war experiments.
The council has moved to allay fears surrounding the long term damage the experimental vaccines would have on those children involved.
The NHMRC's Chairman, Professor Richard Larkins, says trials of cancer and malaria treatments are ongoing, and essential to the advancement of medical knowledge.
He says it would be very destructive if reports such as those about the use of children in experiments stopped peopleparticipating in trials.
The Council has also ruled out an ethics probe into the orphan trials, saying that would not reveal very much.
GOVT DEFENDS ANTI-SMOKING CAMPAIGN
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says smokers want the Government's new anti-smoking campaign.
The tobacco industry claims the campaign is an attempt to distract attention from more crucial community concerns such as jobs, education and health.
Dr Wooldridge told ABC Radio 80% of smokers want to give up and he would expect the tobacco industry to be upset about the campaign.
He says many smokers know the habit is harming them and for every one smoker who says the Government is doing too much to fight smoking, three say it's doing too little.
He says he's fixing that with the Government's biggest ever anti-smoking campaign, in cooperation with state governments, health professionals and community organisations.
POSITIVE OUTLOOK FOR TOURISM: REPORT
A record 4.2 million tourists came to Australia in the year to March.
And a new report shows the number of visitors is set to double in the next decade.
The Tourism Forecasting Council says Asia will still account for the vast majority of tourists.
The strongest growth is tipped to come from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and China.
It's good news for the industry which is experiencing a declining growth of the crucial Japanese market.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
